about.title: Gustine Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Gustine's economy runs on agriculture, food processing, and the small businesses that support both, which means workplace injuries here often involve heavy equipment, delivery vehicles, or work sites shared by multiple contractors. If you were hurt while on the clock, California generally routes your claim through workers' compensation regardless of who was at fault, but that's not always the end of the story. When a piece of faulty equipment, a subcontractor, or another driver on Route 140 or Route 33 contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be available alongside your comp benefits. Because Gustine is a smaller community, injured workers sometimes worry about friction with an employer they know personally, or confusion about deadlines that overlap. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you with an independent attorney familiar with how these dual-track claims work, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Claim

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: California generally makes workers' compensation the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still owe you a separate claim.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: You typically have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your comp benefits.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and Deadlines Run in Parallel
items.desc: An employer cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury, and if a third-party claim applies, it carries its own two-year deadline running alongside your comp case.

items.question: I work on a farm near Gustine and got hurt using equipment owned by a company that isn't my employer. Can I still file a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. If a third party like an equipment manufacturer or a separate contractor contributed to your injury, you may be able to pursue a claim against them in addition to any workers' compensation you receive. An independent attorney can look at who owned or maintained the equipment and whether negligence played a role.

items.question: What happens if my employer in Gustine tells me not to report the injury?
items.answer: Retaliation or discouragement for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California. You generally have 30 days to report the injury to preserve your rights, so it's worth documenting what happened and speaking with an independent attorney as soon as possible.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, our connection service is free, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We're not a law firm ourselves, just the bridge to one.
